condition.text: Rising intracranial pressure with impending herniation

actions.text: Lay the head of the bed flat to rest

parameters.text: Urine specific gravity once a day

questions.stem: On a neurology unit at the start of the shift, four clients have needs. Whose bedside should the nurse go to first?

options.text: A client 2 days after an ischemic stroke who is due for a swallow screen before breakfast
A client with myasthenia gravis whose vital capacity fell from 2.0 to 1.2 L overnight
A client with Parkinson disease whose 0800 levodopa is due in 20 minutes
A client with multiple sclerosis who reports bladder urgency and wants a bedpan

rationale.correct: Declining respiratory muscle strength in myasthenia gravis is the most urgent problem.

perOption.b: Falling vital capacity signals impending respiratory failure.
perOption.c: Time-critical, but there is still time to give it on schedule.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that identify which cranial nerve is affected in each client.

segments.text: Client A cannot close the left eye, with
drooping of the whole left face including the forehead
painful loud sounds in the left ear
no arm or leg weakness and clear speech
brief electric pains in the cheek and jaw triggered by touch or chewing

rationale.correct: Client A has a CN VII (Bell) palsy; client B has CN V neuralgia.

perOption.s2: A peripheral CN VII lesion affects the forehead too.
perOption.s4: CN VII carries taste from the front of the tongue.
perOption.s6: CN VII supplies the stapedius muscle.
perOption.s12: Age is typical but does not identify the nerve.

questions.stem: For each finding, indicate whether it fits Bell palsy or a stroke.

rows.text: Forehead is also weak on the affected side
Arm drift on the same side as the facial droop
Slurred speech and confusion
Isolated facial weakness that developed over a day
Altered taste on the front of the tongue

rationale.correct: Forehead involvement and isolated facial weakness point to Bell palsy; limb or speech signs point to stroke.

questions.stem: Client B returns 3 weeks after starting carbamazepine. Review the findings. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

exhibits.title: Neurology clinic
exhibits.body: A 61-year-old client with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis diagnosed 2 years ago now has slurred speech, weak hands, and trouble swallowing thin liquids, and has lost 6 kg in 3 months. The client sleeps propped on 3 pillows and wakes with headaches. Thinking and memory are unaffected. The client says, "I don't want to end up on a machine, but I'm not ready to die."

exhibits.title: Primary care
exhibits.body: Client A, 34, woke today unable to close the left eye, with drooping of the whole left side of the face, including the forehead. Taste is altered and loud sounds hurt the left ear. No arm or leg weakness; speech is clear. Client B, 66, has sudden stabbing, electric pains in the right cheek and jaw lasting seconds, set off by chewing, brushing teeth or a breeze; the client has stopped eating and lost 3 kg.

caseStudies.title: TIA, carotid endarterectomy and statin therapy

exhibits.title: Emergency department and vascular unit
exhibits.body: A 68-year-old client had 20 minutes of right hand weakness and trouble finding words this morning; it has fully resolved. The client smokes, has hypertension and diabetes, and stopped atorvastatin a year ago because of muscle aches. Carotid ultrasound: 80% narrowing of the left internal carotid artery.
